'''Clifford P. Kubiak''' is an American inorganic chemist, currently a Distinguished Professor in Chemistry and Biochemistry and the [[Harold Urey|Harold C. Urey]] Chair in Chemistry at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://kubiak.ucsd.edu/kubiak.html|title=Kubiak Research Group}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www-chem.ucsd.edu/faculty/profiles/kubiak_clifford_p.html|title=Kubiak, Clifford}}</ref> Over the course of his career, Kubiak has published over 200 scientific articles.<ref name=":1" /> He has also received the [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Inorganic Chemistry,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-in-inorganic-chemistry.html|title=ACS Award in Inorganic Chemistry|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref>  and is a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and American Chemical Society.<ref name=":1" />
In 2020 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scripps.ucsd.edu/news/five-uc-san-diego-professors-elected-national-academy-sciences|title = Five UC San Diego Professors Elected to National Academy of Sciences| date=29 April 2020 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kubiak grew up in [[Connecticut]], and displayed an interest in chemistry from an early age.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i2/ACS-Award-Inorganic-Chemistry.html|title=ACS Award in Inorganic Chemistry|last=Heldari|first=Nader|website=Chemical & Engineering News}}</ref>

In 1975, Kubiak received his bachelor's degree with honors in chemistry from [[Brown University]]. He also received a Ph.D. in chemistry from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1980,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> where he was a Sherman Clarke Fellow and an [[Elon Huntington Hooker]] Fellow.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
After receiving his Ph. D., Kubiak performed [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] with [[Mark S. Wrighton]], where he worked from 1980 to 1981.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> In 1982, Kubiak joined the faculty of [[Purdue University]] as an assistant professor; in 1987, he became an associate professor, before becoming a full professor in 1990.<ref name=":1" /> During this time, he was also named the Robert A. Wheland Visiting Professor at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1997.<ref name=":1" />

In 1998, Kubiak left Purdue University and moved to the University of California, San Diego as the Harold C. Urey Endowed Chair Professor in Chemistry.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> During his time at UCSD, he has also held the position of Chairman of the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry from 2002 to 2006,<ref name=":0" /> and was named Distinguished Professor in Chemistry and Biochemistry in 2008.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In 2012, he was also appointed to the position of Visiting Associate in Chemistry at the [[Joint Center for Artificial Photosynthesis]] (JCAP) at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He was also an Invited Visiting Professor of electrocatalysis at the [[Paris Diderot University]] in 2014,<ref name=":1" /> and has been appointed to additional visiting positions at [[Tohoku University]] and the [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg|University of Erlangen]].<ref name=":0" />

Kubiak has also served on the [[Editorial board|editorial advisory boards]] of several publications, such as ''[[Accounts of Chemical Research]]'', ''[[Inorganic Chemistry (journal)|Inorganic Chemistry]]'', and ''Materials Science in Semiconductor Processing''.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
The Kubiak Research Group at the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry Graduate Program in Materials Science and Engineering currently studies the reduction of carbon dioxide by means of electrocatalysis and photoelectrocatalysis.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://kubiak.ucsd.edu/research.html|title=Kubiak Research Group|website=Current Projects}}</ref> In addition, his team has expanded research regarding electron-transfer reactions, which can be used in the advancement of molecular electronic devices.<ref name=":4" />

=== Contributions to nanoscience ===
Kubiak was involved in the research of [[Nanotechnology|nanoscience]], with a focus on self-assembled monolayers, from its early days in the 1990s.<ref name=":2" /> His work in this field has included research into [[Colloidal gold|gold nanoclusters]] and molecular conductivity.<ref name=":2" />

==== Gold nanoparticles ====
[[File:GoldNanoparticleElectronTransfer.png|left|thumb|334x334px|Electron transfer between discrete Ru<sub>3</sub>O clusters through gold nanoparticles, as pictured, is ultrafast.<ref name=":5"/>]]
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:Ru3OUnitLigand.png|thumb|An Ru<sub>3</sub>O unit, which can be covalently bound at the sulfur atom to a gold nanocluster<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Canzi|first=Gabriele|last2=Kubiak|first2=Clifford P.|date=2011-07-18|title=Mixed-Valence Nanoclusters: Fast Electron Transfer in Mixed-Valence Systems with a Gold Nanoparticle as the Bridge|journal=Small|language=en|volume=7|issue=14|pages=1967–1971|doi=10.1002/smll.201100483|issn=1613-6829|pmid=21656906}}</ref>.]] -->
Among the properties of gold nanoparticles (or NPs) is their conductivity, allowing ultrafast electron transfer.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Canzi|first1=Gabriele|last2=Kubiak|first2=Clifford P.|date=2011-07-18|title=Mixed-Valence Nanoclusters: Fast Electron Transfer in Mixed-Valence Systems with a Gold Nanoparticle as the Bridge|journal=Small|language=en|volume=7|issue=14|pages=1967–1971|doi=10.1002/smll.201100483|pmid=21656906|issn=1613-6829}}</ref> In 2005, Kubiak, along with Gabriele Canzi, used gold NPs to generate a picosecond ground-state electron transfer reaction, marking the first time such a reaction had been performed.<ref name=":5" /> This ground-state electron transfer allowed for the accurate measurement of the resistances of individual carbon-based molecules.<ref name=":5" />

In 2005, J. Catherine Salsman, Tasuku Ito, and Kubiak energetically distinguished the conductive properties of gold nanoclusters and individual molecules by labeling the structures isotopically, and utilized infrared spectroscopy to observe asymmetry.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Salsman|first1=J. Catherine|last2=Kubiak|first2=Clifford P.|last3=Ito|first3=Tasuku|date=2005-03-01|title=Mixed Valence Isomers|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=127|issue=8|pages=2382–2383|doi=10.1021/ja042351+|pmid=15724979|bibcode=2005JAChS.127.2382S |issn=0002-7863}}</ref>

==== Molecular self-assembly ====
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:MonolayerSelfAssembly.png|left|thumb|337x337px|Self-assembly of bipyridyl-based rhenium system monolayers<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tian|first=Weidong|last2=Datta|first2=Supriyo|last3=Hong|first3=Seunghun|last4=Reifenberger|first4=R. G.|last5=Henderson|first5=J. I.|last6=Kubiak|first6=C. P.|date=1997-01-19|title=Resistance of molecular nanostructures|journal=Physica E: Low-dimensional Systems and Nanostructures|volume=1|issue=1-4|pages=304–309|doi=10.1016/S1386-9477(97)00065-9}}</ref>.]] -->
In 1997, Kubiak and colleagues theoretically calculated the current-voltage properties of [[self-assembled monolayer]]s (SAMs) of organic polymers.<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last1=Tian|first1=Weidong|last2=Datta|first2=Supriyo|last3=Hong|first3=Seunghun|last4=Reifenberger|first4=R. G.|last5=Henderson|first5=J. I.|last6=Kubiak|first6=C. P.|date=1997-01-19|title=Resistance of molecular nanostructures|journal=Physica E: Low-dimensional Systems and Nanostructures|volume=1|issue=1–4|pages=304–309|doi=10.1016/S1386-9477(97)00065-9}}</ref> Such properties depend on the equilibrium [[Fermi energy]] and the voltage division factor, ''E<sub>f</sub>'' and ''η'' respectively, as determined by means of [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]] (STM).<ref name=":6" />

=== [[Carbon dioxide]] fixation ===
In 2014, Kubiak and his colleagues from the University of California, San Diego determined the efficiency of an alternate Re<sup>I</sup>(bpy) catalyst complex pathway, an assembled supramolecular system, which can assist in the reduction of CO<sub>2</sub>.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Machan|first1=Charles W.|last2=Chabolla|first2=Steven A.|last3=Yin|first3=Jian|last4=Gilson|first4=Michael K.|last5=Tezcan|first5=F. Akif|last6=Kubiak|first6=Clifford P.|title=Supramolecular Assembly Promotes the Electrocatalytic Reduction of Carbon Dioxide by Re(I) Bipyridine Catalysts at a Lower Overpotential|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=136|issue=41|pages=14598–14607|doi=10.1021/ja5085282|pmid=25226161|year=2014|bibcode=2014JAChS.13614598M }}</ref> Later, his group also lead the work on replacing the scarce Re to the more abundant Mn in the catalyst for CO<sub>2</sub> reduction. It was seen that the reduction of byproduct CO<sub>2</sub>, driven by solar power, wind, or electricity generated by running water, can produce fuels by means of a carbon-neutral energy cycle.<ref name=":7" />

== Non-scientific pursuits ==
In addition to his work in the scientific community, Kubiak has also served as the Faculty Athletics Representative for the Department of Intercollegiate Athletics at the University of California, San Diego, a position he has held since 2007.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news|url=http://www.ucsdtritons.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5800&ATCLID=1179733|title=Cliff Kubiak Bio|work=Official Web Site of UC San Diego Athletics|archive-date=2017-06-19|access-date=2017-06-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170619223014/http://www.ucsdtritons.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5800&ATCLID=1179733|url-status=dead}}</ref> It is in this capacity that Kubiak received the Athletic Department's Meritorious Service Award in June 2013.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.ucsdtritons.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5800&ATCLID=208172460|title=2012-13 Campaign Wraps Up With Annual Athletics Recognition Night|last=UCSD|date=2013-06-06|work=Official Web Site of UC San Diego Athletics}}</ref> He also chairs the Faculty Athletic Board of Advisors at the same university.<ref name=":8" />

== Personal life ==
Kubiak is married, and currently resides with his wife in [[Del Mar, California]].<ref name=":2" />

== Controversies ==
In May 2011, a University of California, San Diego web page attributed to Kubiak was criticized for its use of a racial slur, specifically one targeting people of East Asian descent, as part of a list of “lab rules” supposedly meant to be humorous.<ref name=":9">{{Cite news|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/education/sdut-ucsd-closes-website-over-slur-2011may23-story.html|title=UCSD closes website over slur|date=2011-05-23|work=The San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite news|url=http://ucsdguardian.org/2011/05/26/chem-prof-apologizes-for-website-with-racial-slur/|title=Chem Prof. Apologizes for Website with Racial Slur|date=2011-05-23|work=UCSD Guardian}}</ref> The web page was subsequently removed by UCSD officials; additionally, a statement was issued by [[Suresh Subramani]] and Mark Thiemens, respectively the executive vice chancellor for academic affairs and the dean of physical sciences at UCSD, offering an apology for Kubiak's actions.<ref name=":9" /> Kubiak himself issued an apology as well, claiming that he had no knowledge of the slur's presence on his website but accepting full responsibility regardless.<ref name=":10" />
